sn10.1:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on Mount Inda’s Peak, the haunt of the yakkha Indaka.
sn10.1:1.3: Then the yakkha Indaka approached the Blessed One and addressed him in verse:
sn10.1:2.1: “As the Buddhas say that form is not the soul,
sn10.1:2.2: How then does one obtain this body?
sn10.1:2.3: From where do one’s bones and liver come?
sn10.1:2.4: How is one begotten in the womb?”
sn10.1:3.2: From the kalala comes the abbuda;
sn10.1:3.3: From the abbuda the pesī is produced;
sn10.1:3.4: From the pesī the ghana arises;
sn10.1:3.5: From the ghana emerge the limbs,
sn10.1:4.1: And whatever food the mother eats—
sn10.1:4.2: The meals and drink that she consumes—
sn10.1:4.3: By this the being there is maintained,
sn10.1:4.4: The person inside the mother’s womb.”
